# Knowledge Base: fundamental-theorem-calculus-oq-01-incomplete-01

## Problem Understanding

This is a targeted completion of the gallery proof `fundamental-theorem-calculus-oq-01`. The goal is the Lebesgue fundamental theorem of calculus for absolutely continuous functions: an absolutely continuous function is differentiable almost everywhere and its derivative integrates to the endpoint difference.

## Insights

- Parent proof `fundamental-theorem-calculus-oq-01` provides the foundation.
- Source notes identify one remaining sorry, with line 224 tied to a Cantor function construction.
- The notes flag absolutely continuous function theory as the likely Mathlib gap and suggest checking `MeasureTheory.BoundedVariation` tools.

## Dead Ends

No failed approaches are recorded in the local notes.
